readme: Curated overlay applied to the reviewed integrations.sh snapshot during catalog import.
Keyed by exact canonical MCP URL. Every field is optional: a supplied value wins over the
snapshot, an omitted one falls through to the snapshot exactly as before.
Every entry must be backed by the provider's own current documentation, not inferred from an
aggregator. Use `notes` to record why a value was chosen so the reasoning survives review.
`featured` promotes an entry to the top of the connector catalog. `official` means the MCP
server is published by the provider on its own domain. Neither is a security review, and
neither may be presented as one.
`identities` sets only a well-known service's display name and logo source, so it never
shows a raw hostname or a generated letter. An identity does not curate, feature or promote
the row, does not change its tier, auth or tools, and keeps its Community label. Back each
name with the provider's own site or documentation and each logo with a licensed source,
recorded in `notes`. Identity logos are vendored like curated ones (catalog:vendor-logos).

entries.name: Gmail
entries.description: Search and read Gmail, download original messages and attachments, manage drafts and labels, organize mail, import messages, and read mailbox changes and settings through the reviewed Gmail bridge.

presentation.introduction: Let agents work with the Gmail account you choose.

capabilities.title: Find and understand mail
capabilities.description: Search messages and threads, then use them as context for your work.

capabilities.title: Draft and send messages
capabilities.description: Prepare drafts, or send a new message or an existing draft. You choose which actions need approval.

capabilities.title: Organize the mailbox
capabilities.description: Work with labels, drafts, messages, and threads through the reviewed tools.

capabilities.title: Retrieve original files
capabilities.description: Download any attachment or complete original email to the agent filesystem.

capabilities.title: Monitor and inspect Gmail
capabilities.description: Read mailbox changes, account settings and configuration. Optional notifications use an operator-configured Pub/Sub topic.

presentation.permissionSummary: Google first asks only to read the mailbox you approve. If you later ask an agent to draft, send or organize mail, it asks you in the chat to allow that too. Choose Allow, Ask first, or Block for the available tools in Approvals. Models paid with Opengeni credits do not train on your mail. If agents run on your own AI subscription, turn off model training in that provider's settings first.

https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.re.label: Read your mail
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.re.description: Search and read messages and threads in the account you approve.

https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.co.label: Draft and send messages
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.co.description: Create drafts and send mail using your selected approval settings.

https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.mo.label: Organize your mailbox
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.mo.description: Manage labels, drafts and mailbox organization, move mail to Trash or restore it, and import messages.

notes: scopesHint is what a first connection asks for: read access only. gmail.compose and gmail.modify are asked for later through incremental consent, when a tool call needs them, and never beyond the reviewed Gmail REST tools. OAuth discovery uses pinned Google metadata and verifies the consenting mailbox with Gmail users/me/profile, without depending on the Developer Preview MCP server. Gmail connections are personal-only; every member connects their own mailbox.

allowedTools freezes the reviewed tool surface. Every tool call executes through Opengeni's first-party Gmail REST bridge (packages/runtime/src/gmail-rest-mcp.ts), never Google's Developer Preview MCP endpoint directly; this connection's mcpUrl identity is unchanged so existing consents and reconnect flows keep working. send_message and send_draft use the selected account's approval choices; requireApproval supplies the recommendation when no choice is saved.

logoSourceUrl is null because Google has not published a reusable Gmail MCP logo asset, so nothing is vendored or hotlinked. @opengeni/react bundles the Gmail product mark (packages/react/src/assets) and shows it for this MCP URL.

presentation.permissionSummary: Atlassian asks you to approve access to the sites you choose. Agents only see what your Atlassian account can see. If connecting fails with a domain or policy error, an Atlassian organization admin must allow the Opengeni domain for the Rovo MCP server in Atlassian Administration.

notes: Atlassian's recommended v2 endpoint. ?tools=all is Atlassian's documented, non-secret switch to a flat tool list instead of discover and execute gateway tools, so every tool keeps its own approval policy; it is the one reviewed query string in REVIEWED_QUERY_MCP_URLS.
Same authorization server as v1. A v1 token can't call v2, so v1 and v2 connections stay separate resources; the v1 row stays for existing connections.
Keyed to jira.com like the v1 row. Not marked official for the same reason: mcp.atlassian.com is not mechanically checkable against the snapshot domain jira.com.

Logo: Simple Icons "atlassian" (CC0-1.0 icon data, Atlassian's brand blue). The registry's jira.com asset is the full Atlassian wordmark, which is unreadable in a square tile. The mark remains Atlassian's and identifies the service by nominative use.

entries.description: See what's on your calendar, check when you're free, and add, move or cancel events in your Google Calendar.

presentation.introduction: Let agents work with the Google Calendar you choose.

capabilities.title: Answer questions about your schedule
capabilities.description: See what's on today, tomorrow or any week, in your own time zone.

capabilities.title: Find free time
capabilities.description: Check when you, or people who share their calendar with you, are free.

capabilities.title: Add and change events
capabilities.description: Create, move, update or delete events. You choose which actions need approval.

presentation.permissionSummary: Google asks to see your list of calendars, see and edit events, and see when you are free or busy. Choose Allow, Ask first, or Block for each tool in Approvals.

https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.label: See your list of calendars
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.description: See which calendars you have and their time zones.

https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.label: See and edit events
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.description: Read events and add, change or delete them using your approval settings.

https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.label: See when you're free or busy
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.description: Check free and busy times on calendars you can see.

notes: scopesHint is the least-privilege set for the reviewed tools: calendar-list read, events read/write and free/busy. The broad calendar and calendar.readonly scopes are deliberately not requested. OAuth discovery uses pinned Google metadata and verifies the consenting account with calendarList/primary. Google Calendar connections are personal-only; every member connects their own calendar.

allowedTools freezes the reviewed tool surface. Every tool call executes through Opengeni's first-party Calendar REST bridge (packages/runtime/src/google-calendar-rest-mcp.ts) against the Calendar v3 API, never Google's hosted Calendar MCP endpoint, whose URL is kept only as the connection identity. create_event, update_event and delete_event use the selected account's approval choices; requireApproval supplies the recommendation when no choice is saved.

logoSourceUrl is null because Google has not published a reusable Calendar MCP logo asset, so nothing is vendored or hotlinked. @opengeni/react bundles Google's Calendar product mark (packages/react/src/assets) and shows it for this MCP URL.
